title: Barrels rolled by grossbooted draymen out of Prince’s stores.
html_source:
Note the alternation from the men making the barrels thud to the passive structure of the barrels being rolled by the draymen. The parrallel structure of these three lines suggests a possible reference to Aeolus.

The Aeolian harp
is an instrument that is played by the wind. Hence the active force making the music is absolutely ignorant of its own creation and the instrument is the real artist.

In this sequence it is suggested that the same holds for men, as they ‘make the barrels thud’ while in fact the barrels do the thudding themselves, and the draymen are merely the ignorant ‘force’ behind their music.
